text:
Marta: Quick heads-up — I'm planning to enable the feature flag `route.sticky_v2` for a tiny canary (5% sessions) across EU + APAC to validate multi-region failover behavior. Doing this at 12:00 UTC. Please shout if any blocked assumptions.
Alex: Ack. Do we have a clear fallback order if eu nodes get saturated?
Marta: Good call — fallback order for the canary is: 1) same region, different model-variant 2) fallback region `us-east-1` with quantized variant 3) degrade to short responses. Config snippet below.
Priya: Paste the flag payload so I can verify the console config matches infra routing. Also: will this change sticky key from session->user? That affects KV cache hit rates.
Marta: Putting snippet here:
```
flag: route.sticky_v2
scope:
  regions: ["eu-west-1","ap-northeast-1"]
  audience: 5%
fallback_policy: ["same-model-variant","region:us-east-1","model: rwd-3b-quant"]
stickiness: user
cache_affinity: user_id
metrics: ["latency.p50","kv.hit_rate"]
```
Sam: Looks fine. Note: cache_affinity=user_id will reduce cold KV misses but could increase memory pressure per-worker. Recommend watching `kv.mem.usage` during ramp.
Marta: Thanks — I'll add a temporary autoscale floor for the canary pools just in case.
Alex: Two asks: 1) add fallback metric alert for >5% routed to us-east 2) disable stickiness quickly via the same flag if we see KPI regressions.
Marta: Will add alerts. What's the quick toggle key? Is it `route.sticky_v2.enabled`?
Priya: Yes — `route.sticky_v2.enabled: false` will kill stickiness but keep rollout config.
deploy-bot: Canary toggle scheduled by Marta at 2024-06-28 12:00 UTC — flag: route.sticky_v2, audience:5%, regions: eu-west-1, ap-northeast-1. Link: https://console/internal/flags/route.sticky_v2
ops-bot: Note: autoscale floor added to eu canary pool +30% for 30m window.
Sam: If anything looks off, please ping #eng-oncall and I'll hop on.
Marta: Appreciate it. I'll start the rollout in ~10m and post results (latency, kv.hit_rate, fallback-routes) in this thread. :rocket:
